paragraphs: R' Yaakov (supplied בירה; Hyman’s printed text has בריה, “his son”) — Sheviit 2:4.

notes.text: The connected Hyman notice on Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye tentatively identifies him with Yaakov bar Abaye of Bardelia and cites the same Sheviit 2:4. This supports the proposed son-reading, but the supplied word בירה remains uncertain.

The supplied short pointer says R' Yaakov and בירה at Sheviit chapter2 halakhah4. No whole named Sheviit text or connected Hyman notice was newly read this wake; the older connected-notice comparison remains historical context, not primary passage or printed-letter proof. Without exact-passage full-title support, the abbreviated title stays R'. The current POSSIBLY transposed בריה, his son, remains explicitly possible, with no replacement of בירה, invented Bira byname/place, certain son relationship or automatic link from the Abaye heading. Abaye di-Bardalya in the title remains the supplied heading's contextual transliteration, not an admitted father identity. The current note and original mixed note, all three English versions and the root's finite correction remain exact. Only this qualification is appended; p001 remains held without Hebrew repair, note retirement, identity admission or publication.

Hyman’s printed pointer (vol. I, p. 87) reads בריה, “his son,” where the supplied Wikisource transcription has בירה. The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 2:4 names Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye de-Bar Delayya in the ruling about keeping a planting after its planter dies. Guggenheimer renders the last element “from Bar Delaiah.” Hyman’s separate entry on Rabbi Yaakov bar Abaye (vol. II, p. 773) considers that identification very likely and treats the proposal that he was the son of Abaye the colleague of Rava as difficult. The comparison leaves those identifications open.
